**ACRA XBRL financial statement filing requirements and exemptions** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** ACRA says all Singapore-incorporated companies must prepare financial statements, except dormant relevant companies, and must file them unless exempted. The Full/Simplified/FSH/PDF template depends on the company’s exact status and regulatory category. Dormant relevant companies need not prepare/file only if all Companies Act section 201A requirements are met, including the assets, dormancy and listing/subsidiary conditions. A solvent EPC meeting an EPC definition may elect not to file financial statements but may file voluntarily; its annual-return solvency declaration still applies. Foreign companies with Singapore branches and some individually approved cases are addressed elsewhere on the ACRA filing guidance and are not classified by this local-company rule summary. A case-specific conclusion requires: Local/foreign incorporation, company form and whether it is a company limited by guarantee. Required-to-file/exempt status, dormancy history, listed/subsidiary status and group assets. Current-year revenue and assets, consolidation and currency facts. The Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month for all employees. It was gradually raised and has reached $8,000 in 2026. From 1 Sep to 31 Dec 2023 | $6,300 (+$300)

From 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025 | $7,400 (+$600)

The AW ceiling determines the maximum amount of AW subject to CPF contributions for the year. An employee’s AW ceiling is computed on a
per employer, per year basis. The AW ceiling applies to all Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR).
AW ceiling Calculation
The AW ceiling is computed using the following formula:
$102,000 - Total Ordinary Wages (OW) subject to CPF for the year
For the year 2026, the AW ceiling is
$102,000 – ($8,000* x 12)
* The OW ceiling is capped at $8,000 for 2026.
